outputPerAnimal.notes: National commercial broiler industry average, South Africa, 2022. A separate breed-trial table (Table 4b, same document, p.39) gives named-strain 'Cumulative FI (kg)' and 'Body weight (kg)' at exactly 35 days: Arbor Acres Plus 2.29kg, Cobb 500 2.52kg, Indian River 2.30kg, Ross 308 2.30kg (cumulative feed intake 3.21-3.64kg) - a slightly older age (35 vs 32-33 days) and higher weight than the industry-wide average quoted above; not merged into the primary figure since it is a different (breed-standard trial) dataset, but used below for the feed-intake figure.

seasonalPattern.notes: No SA source found making an explicit year-round or seasonal claim specific to broiler meat production (unlike the layer lighting-program statement); broilers are reared in enclosed, climate-controlled houses on a fixed ~32-35 day cycle in the sources used, with no discussion of calendar-month variation.

evidence.quote:
Average slaughter age is 
now 32 – 33 days at a weight of 1.8 – 1.85 kg.
evidence.doc: SAPA Industry Profile 2022, section 6.9 Performance efficiency

timeToFirstProductWeeks.notes: 32 days / 7 = 4.57 weeks; 33 days / 7 = 4.71 weeks. This enterprise has a single grow-out cycle ending in slaughter, so 'time to first product' = age at slaughter. South Africa, commercial industry average.

productiveLifeYears.notes: Not applicable to a single-cycle meat enterprise: commercial broilers are reared for one ~32-35 day grow-out cycle and then slaughtered (see timeToFirstProductWeeks/outputPerAnimal), not kept for a multi-year productive life. No source gave a separate figure for parent/breeder stock life, so left null rather than guessed.

feedKgPerAnimalPerDay.notes: Set to null in editor review: a whole-cycle average made by dividing cumulative feed to 35 days by 35; intake rises daily and the source gives no per-day figure. Withdrawn value: [0.092, 0.104].

waterLPerAnimalPerDay.notes: No SA government/research or peer-reviewed source found giving a litres/day water-intake figure for broilers specifically (the SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production discusses water ACCESS/hygiene requirements - see welfare - but not a quantified daily intake volume, and the SAPA Industry Profile 2022 does not give one either). Searched sapa-cop-broilers.pdf and sapa-industry-profile-2022.pdf full text for 'water' + intake figures without finding a quantified value.

spaceM2PerAnimal.notes: Set to null in editor review: derived by dividing a 40 kg/m² biomass limit by a slaughter weight from another section; kept instead as a welfare point in the source's own terms. Withdrawn value: [0.045, 0.046].

welfare.point: Floor-housed broilers: no more than 40 kg of bird per square metre.

evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012), 2.2 Housing of broilers in Floor Systems

welfare.point: Newly hatched chicks must be given feed within 24 hours of hatching.

evidence.quote: Newly hatched broiler chicks must be provided with food within 24 hours of hatching.
evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012)

welfare.point: Newly hatched chicks must be given access to water within 24 hours of hatching, sooner in hot weather.

evidence.quote:
Newly hatched broiler chicks should receive water within 24 hours of hatching but sooner during hot 
weather.
evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012)

welfare.point: Fresh water and the right feed always available, so birds are free from hunger and thirst.

evidence.quote: Free from hunger and thirst via the availability of fresh water and the appropriate feed.
evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012)

welfare.point: Broiler houses need a minimum ventilation/airflow rate of 5 cubic metres per hour for every kilogram of bird mass in the house.

evidence.quote:
minimum airflow of 5 cubic 
meters per hour per kg of bird mass is required.
evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012)

welfare.point: In free-range broiler production, indoor stocking must not exceed 15 birds per square metre of floor space.

evidence.quote: stocking density of 15 broiler birds per square meter of available floor space is permitted.
evidence.doc: SAPA Code of Practice for Broiler Production (May 2012), 2.4 Free Range Broiler Production

legal.point: An owner or manager whose animals are, or may be, infected with a controlled animal disease must report it to the state veterinary director immediately.

evidence.quote:
have become or can reasonably be suspected of having become infected with any controlled
animal disease, immediately report such incidence in the prescribed manner to the director.

legal.point: Newcastle disease and notifiable avian influenza are on the state list of controlled and notifiable animal diseases.

evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Controlled and Notifiable Animal Diseases (factsheet)

legal.point: No animal may be slaughtered anywhere but an abattoir, with the exceptions below.

evidence.quote: slaughter any animal at any place other than an abattoir;

legal.point: Slaughter for your own household, or for cultural or religious purposes, is exempt from the abattoir rule.

evidence.quote:
Subsection (1) does not apply to slaughter for own consumption or for cultural
or religious purposes.

gaps: No litres/day water-intake figure for broilers could be sourced from SAPA's Code of Practice or Industry Profile (both discuss water access/quality requirements but not a quantified daily volume); FAO general poultry material was not used as a substitute since a labelled 'FAO (general, not SA-specific)' broiler water figure was not found either.

No explicit statement of year-round or seasonal production specific to broilers (as opposed to layers, where SAPA Layer Notes explicitly states lighting keeps production level 'throughout the year') was found; broilers are reared on a fixed ~32-35 day indoor cycle in all sources used, with no discussion of calendar-month variation, so productionMonths/seasonalPattern are left empty/null.
productiveLifeYears is not applicable to this single-cycle meat enterprise (see notes) and was not populated with a guessed figure.

nda.gov.za and dalrrd.gov.za were unreachable for the Animal Diseases Act (connection reset / 502 on every attempted URL, consistent with this being a known-flaky host); an eccogta.gov.za (Eastern Cape district) mirror of the same Act text was used instead and verified to match the original page count and content.

Editor review 2026-09-28: feed withdrawn (a cumulative-to-35-days figure divided by 35); space withdrawn (a 40 kg/m² limit divided by a weight from another section) and kept as a welfare point in kg/m². Legal: dropped the Act's general definition (the factsheet point names avian influenza and Newcastle) and trimmed summaries beyond their quotes.
